attacks.claim: The agreed constraint requires all customer documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings, prompts) to be stored and processed in the EU under DPAs. The plan moves ~41M chunks and embeddings into Nimbus Vector Store, which is provisioned only in us-east-2, so customer-derived data would be stored outside the EU in breach of DPAs.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap."

attacks.claim: Only the generation region is stated (Dublin). The region and sub-processor terms for embed-3, which receives raw chunk text from ingest workers, and for logs are not established. ZDR coverage of the embed and Vector Store paths is also not stated.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: region, sub-processor and ZDR coverage for embed-3 and Vector Store; only "region eu-west-1 (Dublin)" for generation.

attacks.claim: Quality parity is asserted from 25 support-inbox questions with two lawyers judging. This is far too small to support the claim for legal QA. The plan explicitly defers the 4,100-case regression suite, which is the agreed release gate for any model change, to week 6+, after cutover.
attacks.evidence: "This confirms quality parity or better, so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: Week 3 releases the GPU reservation and deletes the fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters, and Week 5 removes pgvector and the vLLM manifests, all before the regression suite has validated the Nimbus stack. Rollback is destroyed first. Deleting the fine-tuned weights is an irreversible one-way door.
attacks.evidence: "release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage" / "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: LoRA adapter behaviour is replaced by system prompts that are drafted in week 1. No evaluation against the adapters is planned before cutover, so the behaviour change in legal answers is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Re-embedding is a bulk backfill of ~41M chunks in week 2, while only new documents are dual-written. Documents ingested or changed during the backfill, and the consistency check before the week 4 cutover, are not addressed. There is no validation of retrieval parity between pgvector and the new store.
attacks.evidence: "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: The latency measurement is a single 1,000-request sample from Frankfurt, while the stated region is Dublin. It is not stated whether the test was run against the production configuration.
attacks.evidence: "measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05)"

attacks.claim: Generation, embeddings and retrieval all move to one proprietary provider. The plan deletes the fine-tuned weights, adapters and pgvector, and has no exit or fallback path. The embedding space also changes, so reverting later means re-embedding everything.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: exit or fallback plan; "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters"

attacks.claim: A preview-tier Vector Store becomes the sole retrieval path. The plan has no stated failure handling, SLA, or alerting for Nimbus outages, even though the existing stack is removed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: failure handling, alerting, or SLA for Nimbus.

attacks.claim: The generation estimate of $7,900 is given without token or volume math, and 200k-context usage could raise it. The 6.2 TB storage line is closed out while only $140 is tabulated. This is not blocking, since the savings margin is large.
Tenant isolation depends on per-tenant collections and scoped keys in a preview service. Their enforcement is not verified, and there is no cross-tenant leakage test.
attacks.evidence: "one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key"
